title: The Lucena bridge
tagline: Rook to the fourth, king walks out, wall goes up

principles.prompt: Rook ending: your pawn on the 7th, your king stuck on the queening square, checks incoming. What's the plan?
principles.answer: Build the bridge: rook to the fourth rank, king steps out into the checks, and when the king reaches the fifth the rook interposes. Checks over, pawn queens.

principles.prompt: Why does the bridge rook go to the fourth rank exactly?
principles.answer: The king walks down to the fifth. A rook on the fourth is one step below — ready to block the final check and stand guard while the pawn promotes.

principles.prompt: You're defending rook vs rook-and-pawn. Name Philidor's two-part plan.
principles.answer: Rook on your third rank so their king can't cross; the moment the pawn steps onto that rank, drop the rook behind them and check forever — their king has no shelter.

demos.title: Building the bridge
demos.intro: The Lucena position: pawn on the 7th, king boxed in front of it, enemy rook ready to check forever. Watch the bridge go up.

steps.note: The bridge: the rook takes the fourth rank and waits. Its moment comes last.
Black can only wait too — the checks begin when the king steps out.
— and down. The king zigzags toward the rook's rank.
Black keeps checking; there's nothing better.
The fifth rank — one step above the waiting rook.
…meets the bridge. The rook blocks, the checks are over, and b8=Q cannot be stopped.
— and the pawn queens next move. Rook to the fourth, king to the fifth, wall between: that's Lucena.

demos.title: Philidor holds the door
demos.intro: The defender's mirror. Black's rook patrols the sixth rank — White's king may not cross.

steps.note: — and back. The rook on the sixth is what matters, not the king.
The rook keeps the sixth-rank patrol. White's king still can't cross.
The pawn takes the sixth — the rank the rook was renting. Now the plan flips:
Straight to the first rank. The pawn that evicted the rook also blocks its own king's shelter.
Nowhere to hide: e7 belongs to Black's king.
Forever. Rook on the third rank until the pawn crosses, then checks from behind: Philidor, and it holds.

tests.title: Complete the bridge
tests.intro: The king has walked the gauntlet to the fifth rank and the checks found him one last time. Finish it.

wrong.Kc6: Step off the b-file and Rxb7 erases the pawn — every king move abandons it. Block the check instead.
wrong.Kc5: Step off the b-file and Rxb7 erases the pawn — every king move abandons it. Block the check instead.
wrong.Ka5: Step off the b-file and Rxb7 erases the pawn — every king move abandons it. Block the check instead.
wrong.Ka6: Step off the b-file and Rxb7 erases the pawn — every king move abandons it. Block the check instead.

hints: The rook has been waiting on the fourth rank this whole time. This is its moment.
Rb4 — the bridge closes. If the rooks trade, your king recaptures and the pawn queens.

tests.explanationAfter: The bridge in one frame: the interposed rook ends the checks and shields the king. Trading was Black's best — after Kxb4 nothing on the board can reach b8 in time.

tests.title: Bridge, southbound
tests.intro: Your bridge this time, heading down the board. The last check has just landed.

wrong.Kf4: Leave the g-file and Rxg2 erases the pawn — half a point gone. The waiting rook blocks instead.
wrong.Kh4: Leave the g-file and Rxg2 erases the pawn — half a point gone. The waiting rook blocks instead.
wrong.Kf3: Leave the g-file and Rxg2 erases the pawn — half a point gone. The waiting rook blocks instead.
wrong.Kh3: Leave the g-file and Rxg2 erases the pawn — half a point gone. The waiting rook blocks instead.

hints: Same picture as the last drill, rotated: your rook on f5 has been waiting for exactly this check.
Rg5 — block, invite the trade, recapture, queen.

tests.explanationAfter: Colour-blind again: rook to the (defender's) fourth, king to the fifth, wall between. After Kxg5 the g-pawn touches down and White's king is a spectator.
